title: Rational numbers
competency: Describe rational numbers, tell kinds of fractions apart and write fractions in simplest form.

keywords.def: A number that can be written a/b with integers a, b and b ≠ 0. The set is written ℚ.
A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator, such as 3/4.
A fraction whose numerator is at least its denominator, such as 7/3.
A whole number with a proper fraction, such as 5¼.
a/b is in simplest form (lowest terms) when GCF(a, b) = 1.
Numbers whose GCF is 1, such as 8 and 15.

en.text: Dividing one integer by another does not always give an integer. So we use a bigger set. A rational number can be written a/b, where a and b are integers and b is not 0. Every integer is rational, because n = n/1.

am.text: አንድን ኢንቲጀር በሌላ ማካፈል ሁልጊዜ ኢንቲጀር አይሰጥም። ስለዚህ ትልቅ ስብስብ እንጠቀማለን። ምክንያታዊ ቁጥር a/b ተብሎ ሊጻፍ ይችላል፤ a እና b ኢንቲጀሮች ሲሆኑ b ዜሮ አይደለም። እያንዳንዱ ኢንቲጀር ምክንያታዊ ነው፤ ምክንያቱም n = n/1 ነው።

screens.title: Divide some integers
screens.text: Take the integers 7, −2, 6, 0 and −3. Try these four divisions: 6 ÷ (−3), 0 ÷ 7, 7 ÷ 6 and −2 ÷ 7.
screens.ask: How many of the four answers are integers? Take a guess.
screens.after: Read on to see which answers are integers.

screens.title: Activity 1.9: what happens?
paras: But 7 ÷ 6 = 7/6 and −2 ÷ 7 = −2/7. These are not integers.
Dividing integers does not always give an integer. So we need a bigger set: the rational numbers.

screens.title: Definition 1.5 · Rational numbers
paras: A number that can be written as a/b is a rational number. Here a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
The set of rational numbers is ℚ = {a/b : a, b ∈ ℤ and b ≠ 0}.
−6 = −6/1 and 0 = 0/1. So every integer is rational. So is every natural number: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ.
screens.note: Figure 1.2: natural numbers sit inside the integers, which sit inside the rational numbers.

ideas.name: Kinds of fractions and simplest form

en.text: In a proper fraction the top is smaller than the bottom, like 7/8. In an improper fraction the top is at least the bottom, like 7/3. A mixed fraction is a whole number with a proper fraction, like 5¼. A fraction is in simplest form when top and bottom have GCF 1.

am.text: በትክክለኛ ክፍልፋይ ላዩ ከታቹ ያንሳል፤ ለምሳሌ 7/8። ትክክለኛ ባልሆነ ክፍልፋይ ላዩ ቢያንስ ከታቹ እኩል ነው፤ ለምሳሌ 7/3። ድብልቅ ክፍልፋይ ሙሉ ቁጥርና ትክክለኛ ክፍልፋይ ነው፤ ለምሳሌ 5¼። የላይና የታች ትልቁ የጋራ አካፋይ 1 ሲሆን ክፍልፋዩ በቀላሉ ቅርጽ ነው።

screens.title: Note: kinds of fractions
paras: Let x = a/b be a fraction with a and b positive.
(i) If a < b, x is a proper fraction.
(ii) If a ≥ b, x is an improper fraction.
(iii) A whole number with a proper fraction, such as 5¼, is a mixed fraction.
Example 2. 7/8 and 2/9 are proper. 7/3 and 6 (= 6/1) are improper. 5¼ is mixed.
screens.note: The book states (i) and (ii) for any integers a and b. They are meant for positive numbers: by the book's rule, −5/2 would count as proper because −5 < 2.

screens.title: Simplest form
paras: (iv) x = a/b is in simplest form (lowest terms) when GCF(a, b) = 1.
That is, a and b are relatively prime.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Numerator smaller than denominator, such as 7/8.

A whole number with a proper fraction, such as 5¼.
a/b with GCF(a, b) = 1. Also called lowest terms.

screens.title: Mixed to improper
screens.text: Change a mixed fraction to an improper fraction: l m/n = l + m/n = (l × n + m)/n.
steps: Start with 3¼. Here l = 3, m = 1 and n = 4.
Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 3 × 4 = 12.

items.text: 3. Zebiba measures a table as 54 cm and 4 mm.
items.ask: In centimetres, in lowest terms, this is ___ cm.

items.text: 4. A rope 5⅓ m long is cut into 4 equal pieces.
items.clue: Change 5⅓ to an improper fraction first.
items.worked: 5⅓ = 16/3. Then 16/3 ÷ 4 = 16/12 = 4/3. So each piece is 1⅓ m.

notes.text: Kinds of fractions: the book states (i) and (ii) for any integers a and b. They are meant for positive numerators and denominators: by the book's rule, −5/2 would count as proper because −5 < 2.
Exercise 1.10 item (c) in the printed book does not say b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0. Without that, a/b and c/d might not be numbers. The lesson adds the condition.
Exercise 1.10 Q2 (show that a product of rationals is rational) is a proof and is not turned into an item.

screens.title: Find GCF(18, 24)
